mismatch.message: Replay error: OBJ_BURIED is not defined

summary: The case reaches the carried-boulder burial branch of mon.c:xkilled. JavaScript mirrors the C pit and inventory predicates and passes CORPSTAT_BURIED to make_corpse(), whose bury_an_obj() call buries the corpse. It then evaluates cadaver.where === OBJ_BURIED before printing C's visible buried-corpse message, but js/mon.js does not import OBJ_BURIED. The missing binding stops the replay at that condition; import the existing obj.h enum constant and preserve the C message guard.

callers: mon.c:make_corpse -> bury_an_obj when CORPSTAT_BURIED is set
findings: mon.c:xkilled checks mtrapped, finds a pit at the monster coordinates, and sets burycorpse when m_carrying(mtmp, BOULDER) succeeds (lines 3514-3522).
The ordinary corpse path passes CORPSTAT_BURIED to make_corpse when burycorpse is true (lines 3617-3628).
The buried-corpse message is conditional on the returned corpse being OBJ_BURIED and visible, matching the source state transition and message guard.

js/mon.js imports CORPSTAT_BURIED and implements the corresponding make_corpse/bury_an_obj path, but its constants import list omits OBJ_BURIED while xkilled reads it at the message guard. js/const.js already exports OBJ_BURIED as the C obj.h enum value 6.
The admitted evaluation reports an immediate ReferenceError before any replay steps; this is a missing binding, not evidence of different random or burial behavior.

evidence: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/mon.c:xkilled. The pit guard at lines 3514-3522 sets burycorpse only when the monster is trapped over a pit and carries a boulder; the corpse branch at lines 3617-3628 passes CORPSTAT_BURIED and tests cadaver->where == OBJ_BURIED before its message.

Read js/mon.js:xkilled and make_corpse. JavaScript has the same carried-boulder predicate, awaits make_corpse(CORPSTAT_BURIED), and compares cadaver.where to OBJ_BURIED, but the top-level imports do not bind OBJ_BURIED.
Read js/const.js:1196, which exports OBJ_BURIED = 6, and js/bury.js:bury_an_obj, which is the existing helper used by make_corpse when burythem is true.
The admitted v74 evaluation identifies the first stop as ReferenceError 'OBJ_BURIED is not defined'; the source comparison pinpoints the missing js/mon.js import at the message guard.
